messages:
incident-bot: P1 pager — enterprise tenant 'Marlin' seeing sustained 50-70% request error rate from us-east1 dedicated pool. Alerts: backend 5xx spike, KV auth errors, elevated latency. Auto-escalation to oncall.
alex_sre: got it. I'm on call. Triage in progress, assigning Maya for routing and Jon for infra. Priya flagging customer.
maya: looking at traces — errors appear at the load balancer -> auth proxy hop. KV auth timeouts 500-1000ms. Could be degraded warm instances or network to tenant VPC.
jon_platform: checking pool health. Dedicated GPUs in us-east1 show 2/8 nodes with high OOM/restarts. Autoscaler didn't replace fast enough. Pulling recent deploys.
sam_network: no infra-wide network issues from netops. VPC peering metrics show increased retransmits for Marlin's subnet around 3337002100.
priya_acct: PM at Marlin (Rachel) is online, wants ETA and mitigation steps. She confirms clients are seeing spikes in production users.
alex_sre: quick decision tree: 1) isolate tenant traffic to alternate warm pool in us-east1b, 2) shift DNS to warm pool edge for Marlin (TTL 60) if isolation insufficient, 3) prepare cross-region shift to us-west1 as fallback. Who can stand up warm pool routing?
maya: I can trigger traffic policy change to route Marlin to pool-us-east1b-warm via smart-router. Will validate compatibility with tenant VPC peering first. Command:
```
# switch policy
rwdctl routing update --tenant marlin --from pool-us-east1a --to pool-us-east1b-warm --mode draining --grace 30s
```
alex_sre: good. Jon, can you expand the warm pool capacity by +20% and check KV auth endpoints? We need healthcheck override during migration.
jon_platform: scaling warm pool now. Running:
```
infractl scale pool-us-east1b-warm --add-instances 4
kubectl rollout status deploy/warm-router -n routing
```
jon_platform: warm pool instances booting, ETA ~90s. KV auth endpoint pods show 3/5 with restart counts. I'm adding a kill-switch to route around unhealthy auth replicas.
deploy-bot: deploy event: infra/kvs-auth v2.14.3 rollback triggered by jon_platform at 3337002280.
sam_network: peering route metric improved after moving a subset of flows; still seeing ~10% packet loss on one path. I'll open a temporary SR to cloud provider if it persists.
maya: routing change applied in dry-run, now promoting to live. Starting canary at ~3337002310 for 5% of Marlin traffic.
alex_sre: canary looks stable for first 30s, errors down from 60% -> 12% for canary slice.
priya_acct: told Rachel we have a canary and will expand in 10m if stable. She asked for notification when DNS TTL cutover happens.
alex_sre: plan: expand to 50% in 2m, full in 5m. If errors spike >20% revert. DNS TTL change is next iff cluster-level issues persist.
jon_platform: warm pool now at +4 instances, auth replicas repaired. Rolling forward to 50%.
maya: expanding to 50% now. Monitoring token auth latency and 5xx rate.
oncall-pager: oncall handoff scheduled in 35 minutes to maya if we don't escalate. Paging standby.
alex_sre: results: 50% slice error rate at 10%. Expanding to 100%.
maya: 100% expansion complete at 3337002360. Global error rate for Marlin down to 6%. KV auth latency back to baseline.
priya_acct: Rachel confirms traffic is healthy from their side. She requests a brief postmortem and timeline.
alex_sre: closing immediate mitigation — routing to warm pool. Next actions: 1) root cause: investigate root cause of OOMs on dedicated nodes (OOM killer logs, recent model changes), 2) follow-up with infra to improve autoscaler thresholds, 3) prepare DNS fallback playbook (low TTL) and test cross-region failover runbook next maintenance window. I'll create the incident ticket and assign owners.
jon_platform: opening infra ticket INF-4721 for OOM investigation and autoscaler tuning.
sam_network: I'll keep SR with provider open for the transient packet loss; will update if it correlates with infra events.
priya_acct: I'll schedule customer follow-up and share incident timeline.
alex_sre: thanks all. Incident mitigated, keeping thread open for RCA updates and handoff notes. :white_check_mark:
